headline: Carmakers are using their car-parts supply chains to start building humanoid robots, Chosunbiz reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the main events (Xpeng's robot line on 8 Aug, its September funding round) are old, and the rest is analysis and plans.
importance_line: Buyers and workers could eventually see cheaper humanoid robots built by car firms, but the claims are company statements and analysts' views, and mass production is still a target.
summary: Chosunbiz reports in an analysis that Chinese carmaker Xpeng, whose automated humanoid robot line in Guangzhou began operating on 8 Aug 2026, says it aims to build 1,000 robots a month by the end of the year and that over 85% of its robot suppliers also supply its cars. Han Jae-kwon, a robotics professor at Hanyang University in South Korea, says carmakers hold much of the humanoid supply chain already, and the piece adds that Hyundai plans Atlas robots in factories from 2028 and Tesla is reportedly vetting Chinese parts makers for its Optimus robot.
notes: Full article read. Underlying Xpeng robot-line launch happened 8 Aug 2026 (before window), so FOLLOW-UP and score lowered 5 to 4 as stale; the main session may judge that this 9 Oct analysis adds enough for the robotics quota. machine_action true only because IRON is described walking off the line at that launch.
